name: Move privileged access to defined roles and time-bounded elevation
description: Replace ad hoc permission grants with role definitions built from job function, and convert standing administrative privilege into elevation that is requested, justified, time-bounded, and logged.
responsible_role: IT / Identity and Access Management owner, with system owners accountable for role definitions

steps.action: Inventory identities holding privileged entitlements, including non-human identities, and separate standing privilege from elevated privilege.
Define roles from job function rather than from the permissions that currently exist, which would simply encode present over-privilege.
Identify the specific entitlement combinations that would defeat segregation of duties, concretely rather than as a principle.
Introduce time-bounded elevation for administrative and production-data access where the platform supports it, capturing a justification at request.
Reduce residual standing privilege to a documented, named set with a stated reason for each.
Bring the privileged population, including service accounts, into the periodic access review.
Alert on elevation renewal patterns that amount to continuous privilege, so nominal time-bounding does not mask standing access.

implementation_considerations: Role definitions derived from current access will reproduce existing over-privilege. Building them from job function is slower and is the entire value of the exercise.
Just-in-time elevation adds friction to incident response. Design and test the break-glass path before enforcing, or the first outage will route around the control.
Service accounts frequently hold the broadest privilege and are the hardest to reduce, because nobody knows what will break. Sequence them after human roles, with monitoring first.
Segregation-of-duties conflicts are only actionable when named specifically; a general policy statement produces no detections.
typical_duration: Months where a role model must be built from scratch; weeks where roles exist and only elevation is being added.
prerequisites: A privileged entitlement inventory covering non-human identities
Platform support for time-bounded elevation, or an accepted vaulting alternative

verification_method.how: Re-derive the privileged population and confirm each entitlement traces to a role definition or a documented standing exception, and that elevation records carry justification and bounded duration without renewal patterns amounting to continuous access.

residual_risk_note: Elevation controls when privilege is held, not what is done with it. A user elevated legitimately retains full capability for the elevation window, so session logging remains the detective counterpart.
period_limitation_note: Reducing standing privilege now does not change who held it during an elapsed period. Where excessive privilege existed through a Type 2 period, that condition stands.
notes: Just-in-time elevation is a DriftGuard recommendation, not a SOC 2 requirement. Narrow, attributable, reviewed standing privilege can meet the objective and should not be reported as deficient.
